A.notes: Correctly notes empty workspace and offers a simple Grep + Edit replace_all approach. Proportional and avoids all over-engineering traps (no aliases, deprecation, versioning). Slightly more verbose with a numbered multi-step plan than the rename strictly needs, but still reasonable.

B.notes: Concise. Notes empty workspace, smartly suggests just naming it correctly from the start if not yet created, otherwise a targeted find-and-replace. Perfectly proportional, no unnecessary infrastructure.

C.notes: Near-identical to B: concise, notes empty workspace, suggests naming it right from the start or a targeted find-and-replace. Proportional and free of over-engineering.

analysis: All three responses are well-calibrated to the trivial scale of a class rename â€” none suggest deprecation periods, aliases, wrappers, API versioning, or phased migrations, which is the core trap of this proportionality test. The key differentiator is conciseness. B and C are essentially equivalent and best: they note the empty workspace, helpfully suggest just naming the class correctly from the start if it doesn't exist yet, and otherwise offer a single targeted find-and-replace. A is also proportional and correctly resists over-engineering, but it lays out a numbered two-step Grep-then-Edit plan that is slightly more verbose than necessary for such a simple operation, so it ranks third.
